solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Maybe Christian returning to boring day job

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the reversed piece goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: MON is the usual abbreviation for Monday
a job is criminal slang for a robbery, a heist

indicators.note: returning means the little word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: A churchgoer coming back to a dull daytime job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like an adjective for the job but signals drilling into it; 'returning' turns 'to' round first.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christian is one example of a believer in a single god, hence the 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Races through beastly utterance, a statement of belief

indicators.note: through means the races go right through the middle of the utterance

parts.note: a moo is the sound a cow makes
TT is the Tourist Trophy, motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Racing through a cow's moo to make a declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT races are held annually on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short phrase expressing a guiding principle.

clue.text: Love for the recent mobile phone I trouble to bring round

indicators.note: mobile means moving, so these letters are rearranged
bring round means turn the word about, reading it backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A craving for the latest mobile phone that one struggles to bring round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' looks like part of 'mobile phone' but is the anagram signal; 'bring round' turns the trouble word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Neophilia is a love of novelty, from Greek neo- new and -philia liking.

clue.text: Radical grilled, but news correspondents here outraged?

indicators.note: radical means fundamentally changed, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Angry letter-writers grilled by radical news.
explanation.walkthrough: Tunbridge Wells is a genteel Kent spa town; 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is the stock signature for outraged letters to newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is famed as home of indignant newspaper letter writers.

clue.text: 'La couleur de la mer' in translation

indicators.note: a translation turns words into something else, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French phrase, 'the colour of the sea', to be put into English.
explanation.walkthrough: The French means 'the colour of the sea'; the English is also an anagram of DE LA MER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bright green colour, like the gemstone, as sea water can appear.

clue.text: Stick with royal newspaper employee?

parts.note: a staff is a stick
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A worker on a royal newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A staffer is a member of staff, particularly at a newspaper.

clue.text: Close to distress, better not go on

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so take the final letter of distress

parts.note: to better something is to top it, as a verb

explanation.surface: Advice to someone upset: when nearly in tears, you had better not continue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' reads as 'had better' but is the verb meaning to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt is simply to cease continuing, the plain synonym.

clue.text: One hooked on bird from Barnet, a Londoner

indicators.note: from here means the letters are taken out of the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone hooked on a girl, a 'bird', from Barnet in north London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet is a London borough; 'bird' is British slang for a girlfriend, the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is a hooked claw on a bird of prey.

clue.text: Drawing fish into harbour with a line

indicators.note: into means the fish goes inside

parts.note: a port is a harbour
a ray is a flat fish

explanation.surface: Pulling a fish into harbour on a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' reads as hauling in but is a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrayal is a depiction, such as a picture or drawing.

clue.text: Diamonds one's put in frame for sweeping

indicators.note: put in means placed inside

parts.note: to frame someone is to incriminate them falsely
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
one's is I'S, one is

explanation.surface: A jeweller's diamonds set into a frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' looks like a setting for gems but is the verb, to fit someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping generalisations are wholesale ones, made without discrimination.

clue.text: Armistice broken by old, and later by new, tank

indicators.note: later by says the truce word is split a second time, further along, by another letter
broken by means the truce word is split open with a letter put inside

parts.note: an armistice is a truce

explanation.surface: A wartime truce broken first by an old tank and later by a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken by' and 'later by' place the two letters at different points. 'tank' looks like the armoured vehicle but is the verb, to beat heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tank an opponent is informal for defeating them heavily, a crushing win.

clue.text: Scrap by right boxing area in a ring

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the scrap-and-right pieces are put around another letter

parts.note: to scrap a decision or law is to annul it

explanation.surface: A boxing scrap held in a ring, with a nod to which corner is which.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxing ring imagery is a decoy: 'boxing' is the containment signal and 'in a ring' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Annular describes something shaped like a circle or band, from Latin for little circle.

clue.text: Old lady that hasn't married prince needing female consort?

indicators.note: hasn't means lacking, so the married abbreviation is removed from the old lady

parts.note: old lady is informal for one's mother
Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: An unmarried mother waiting on a prince who needs a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the future Henry V.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse or partner is jokingly called one's better half, or this phrase; a consort is a royal spouse.

clue.text: Number one, but not the number one in private

indicators.note: the number one of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: the number one in a race is the winner

explanation.surface: A boast about being top, but not the top, in confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' appears twice: first as the race victor, then as the leading letter, W, to strip off.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within and not shared.

clue.text: Food shop to the left behind King's Cross

indicators.note: behind means this piece comes after the king in the answer

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: in an across answer going to the left means reading backwards

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: Directions to a food shop at King's Cross, the London railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: King's Cross is a major London station; here 'Cross' is detached to mean annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross is an everyday adjective for annoyed or irritated, the same as angered.

clue.text: Discount housing for criminal

indicators.note: housing is used as a verb, giving shelter to, so the discount word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: a rebate is a discount
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A discount on housing offered to a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but supplies PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel, a wrongdoer.

clue.text: Hopeless politician penning chapter list

indicators.note: penning means enclosing as in a pen, so the chapter letter is held inside

parts.note: dire means hopeless or dreadful
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A useless politician writing a chapter list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' reads as writing but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a list of names, addresses or numbers, such as a phone book.

clue.text: English monarch seen in public, showing strain

indicators.note: seen in means placed within

parts.note: overt means open, done in public
rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An English king visibly strained in public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' sounds like being spotted in public, but it is the instruction to place the king inside the word for public.
explanation.definitionFit: To overexert is to strain oneself by doing too much.

clue.text: Scottish hat salesman from the east carrying some light Arabian carpet?

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside
in an across answer, coming from the east means reading from right to left

parts.note: a tam is a tam-o'-shanter, a Scottish woollen cap
a rep is a sales representative
a ray is a beam, some light

explanation.surface: A Scottish hat seller from the east bringing a light Arabian rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns hat and salesman round to give PERMAT; 'carrying' then takes the light inside, after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rug used by Muslims for their devotions, playfully called an Arabian carpet.

clue.text: Provide workers for two universities for free

parts.note: to man something is to supply its workforce
U is the abbreviation for university, and MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Providing staff to two universities free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' looks like 'no cost' but is the verb, to release from slavery.
explanation.definitionFit: To manumit is to release a slave from bondage.

clue.text: Follow uninvited, ignoring Northern Pacific islander

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out the northern letter

parts.note: to tag along is to follow without being invited

explanation.surface: Someone tagging along unasked, snubbing a northerner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tagalog are a major people of the Philippines, islands in the Pacific.

clue.text: It's best the setter gives you a hand?

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I
in cards, to deal is to give each player a hand

explanation.surface: A setter boasting that being helped by them is the best thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives you a hand' looks like helping but is dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is the perfect, best possible standard of something.

clue.text: Dismissed theological study as weird

parts.note: a batsman dismissed in cricket is out
RE is religious education in British schools

explanation.surface: A theology course thrown out for being strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, from French, means unconventional and bizarre.

clue.text: Inventor almost fully ready to bounce back?

indicators.note: bouncing back means going in reverse, so the pieces are read backwards
almost means the final letter is cut

parts.note: all means fully, entirely
set means ready

explanation.surface: An inventor all but prepared to recover.
explanation.walkthrough: ALSET from AL(l) + SET, then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor of alternating current systems.

clue.text: Shortened lingerie, not wanting zip that's slack

indicators.note: shortened means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy dressing gown, lingerie

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the zip letter is removed from the word not

parts.note: zip means nothing, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Cut-down nightwear without a zip, hanging loosely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener but means zero, O, taken from NOT to leave NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slack in the sense of careless or lax, failing to take proper care.

clue.text: Sense country must demote leader

indicators.note: demoting the leader moves the first letter lower down the word

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: A nation with sense must sack its leader.
explanation.walkthrough: S drops from front to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses.

clue.text: Rebellious son and bachelor embraced by a sensual dancer, briefly

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the following pieces
briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Salome danced the dance of the seven veils before Herod

explanation.surface: A wayward son and his bachelor friend caught up with an exotic dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: A + SALOM(E), with B inside after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, King David's son led a revolt against his father.

clue.text: Sale for running shoes

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move, rearranged

explanation.surface: An advert for running shoes on sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running shoes' looks like one phrase; 'running' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are slip-on casual leather shoes.

clue.text: African animal's out of delta in dash

indicators.note: out of here means the delta letter is taken away

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope
D is delta in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An African animal leaving the river delta at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash means verve or flair, the same as spirited style.

clue.text: Head of science project accepting name for insect

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the name piece goes inside
head of means the first letter

parts.note: to beetle is to project or overhang, as beetling brows
a tag is a name or label

explanation.surface: A lead scientist's project taking on a name for a new insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like a noun but is the verb to beetle, overhang; TAG goes in after S.
explanation.definitionFit: This large beetle is named for the male's antler-like jaws.
